scenes.headline: Iterators & Generators
scenes.subtitle: Lazy, memory-efficient data streams
scenes.narration: Iterators and generators let you process data one item at a time, which is the foundation of building pipelines that handle datasets far larger than available memory.

scenes.headline: The iterator protocol
items: An iterable defines __iter__ and returns an iterator
An iterator defines __next__ and yields the next value
StopIteration signals the sequence is exhausted
scenes.narration: At its core the protocol is simple: an iterable exposes __iter__, which hands back an iterator, and that iterator exposes __next__, which produces one value each time it is called. When there is nothing left, __next__ raises StopIteration, and that is precisely the signal a for loop watches for to know when to stop.

scenes.headline: List vs Generator

columns.title: Generator
points: Produces one element at a time

scenes.narration: A list computes and stores every element up front, giving you fast indexing and the ability to iterate it repeatedly, at the cost of holding it all in memory. A generator instead computes each value on demand, so its memory footprint stays flat no matter how much data flows through, but it can only be traversed once. Choose lists when you need random access and reuse, and generators when data is large or streaming.

scenes.headline: A generator with yield
scenes.narration: The presence of yield turns this function into a generator. Each time the loop asks for the next line, execution resumes exactly where yield left off, reads one line, and pauses again. Because the file is never loaded whole, this pattern processes a multi-gigabyte log using only a few kilobytes of memory at any moment.

scenes.headline: Composing generator pipelines
scenes.narration: Generators compose into elegant pipelines where each stage lazily pulls from the one before it. Here reading, parsing, and filtering are chained together, yet nothing runs until the final loop demands a value. Data flows through the whole chain one record at a time, so even an enormous file is filtered for errors with a tiny, constant memory footprint.

scenes.headline: Handy tools & pitfalls
items: Generator expressions like (x*2 for x in data) are lazy one-liners
itertools offers islice, chain, and groupby for stream processing
Remember a generator is exhausted after one full pass
scenes.narration: For quick cases, a generator expression gives you the same laziness as a full function in a single line. The itertools module is a treasure chest for streams, with tools like islice for slicing, chain for concatenation, and groupby for aggregation. The one pitfall to internalize is that a generator is single-use: once fully consumed, iterating it again yields nothing.

scenes.text: Generators trade random access for constant memory — they are the default choice for streaming large or unbounded datasets.
scenes.narration: When your data is large, streaming, or unbounded, reach for generators by default. They let you build clean, composable pipelines that scale to any size while sipping memory.
